overview_markdown:
## Overview

Poco positions itself as a safer, more beautiful, and easier-to-use alternative to OpenClaw. Instead of a lightweight gateway bridging chat apps to agents, Poco is a full-stack product: a FastAPI (Python 3.12+) backend, a Next.js 16 frontend, and a Claude Code–powered agent runtime, all deployable via one-click Docker self-hosting or a managed cloud subscription.

Its standout differentiator is **team collaboration**: long-lived servers with channels, DMs, threads, and mentionable persistent agents, plus project management with per-project model, preset, Git repo, and mount defaults. All task execution happens inside an isolated container sandbox, with optional host directory mounting for self-hosted deployments — a meaningfully safer default than running agents directly on the host.

The agentic experience mirrors Claude Code (slash commands, Plan Mode, sub-agents) and adds MCP/Skills extensibility, a built-in browser, background execution with scheduled triggers, and IM integration with DingTalk, Feishu, and Telegram. Recent commits show active hardening — auth redirect fixes, signed workspace file streaming, and visibility-aware access control — though the project is still young (v0.5.7) with a much smaller community than OpenClaw.
